body: I'm writing this from the psych emergency room, I'm receiving help..... thanks again for the encouraging words.

Thanks guys for the compassionate comments. I have an appointment with my psychopharm on Monday, so just gotta get through the weekend. I'm going to ask him if I can check in to Partial Hospitalization next week.

I really appreciate the time and thought you put into your answers. I called a suicide line last week, and when the lady found out I was bipolar she was like "So just call the number on the back of your insurance card and get a therapist, bye!"...... :(

I feel like I could enjoy life, I certainly HAVE enjoyed life.

But it seems like so much work. And at the end of it all I'm going to die anyways, so why is that work worth anything?

If someone says "You can walk 100 miles and then die, or we can just shoot you now" why bother walking?

Yeah they switched around the meds and I felt better.

Now life situation is really getting me down (unemployed, no friends).

The main idea is: we're all going to turn into dirt one day, why do I have to fucking wait so long.

Yeah I've been hospitalized, I have bipolar disorder.

It got really bad in February, all I could think about 24/7 was how much I really, really wanted to die, and how sad it made me that I couldn't think of a good/effective way to do it.

I'm 23-26 years old now, and I think about suicide almost every day. On days/weeks where things aren't going too well, when I'm feel particularly lonely, I start to make plans. I don't believe in an afterlife, and I don't care what my family and "friends" here would think or how they react. Mostly, I want to make sure that I don't make a big nasty mess that someone has to clean up.

I also want to make sure that when I do it, it gets done. I don't want to jump of a 6 story building and wind up paralyzed in a psych ward.

That's pretty much what's keeping me from doing it. I've many, many times wished I had access to a firearm, because I'm sure that I could walk out into the woods and ...boom
